correctness.rationale: The discrete rank cut objective is identical to the original balanced OVL-q. Moving cuts to whole-run boundaries is justified by concavity; grouping s alternating complete runs costs at least floor(s/2), giving ceil((R-1-q)_+/2). Each disjoint 1001001 occurrence permits removing two run boundaries for exactly one minority count. Its nonoverlapping-block count has mean n/448+O(1), variance O(n) under the balanced permutation measure. The exact classical run formulas imply a Gaussian centered at n+1 with variance asymptotic to n/2. Thus the positive residual is realized at the lower bound with probability tending to one, and n^(1/2) rho converges to (Z-t)_+/(2 sqrt 2); the zero-event probability converges to Phi(t). The provided check.py independently checks original DP minimization and combinatorics in finite cases; no unproved infinite conclusion is inferred from computational checks.

value.rationale: When q increases toward n (the typical run-boundary count), the test loses discrimination by saturating at zero: it develops a sharp sqrt(n) critical window, non-Gaussian positive-part limit and a nonvanishing zero atom. This gives a motivated, quantitative complexity/overfitting calibration boundary for the published two-sample overlap test that fixed-q results cannot diagnose. No claim of alternative power or optimal adaptive calibration is made.
